---
title: "Filter rows and add columns"
---

Keep the penguins with a recorded body mass, and add the mass in kilograms
and a size label to each.
[`penguins`](https://github.com/phpstats/datasets#penguins) has size
measurements for 344 penguins near Palmer Station, Antarctica, from 2007 to
2009 (Gorman et al., 2014).

{{< include pages/_filter-and-mutate.md >}}

- `filter()` keeps the rows for which the row closure returns `true`. Two
  penguins have no recorded mass, so 342 rows remain.
- `select()` keeps four columns, and `mutate()` adds one column for each named
  argument.
- A row closure such as `fn ($r) => $r->body_mass_g / 1000` runs once per row
  and reads the row's columns as properties.
- A column expression such as `col('body_mass_g')->ge(4500)` works on the
  whole column, and `if_else()` uses it to pick `'large'` or `'small'`.
- `sex` is NA for some penguins. Missing values print as `<NA>`.

Reference: [Single-table functions](../reference/single-table.qmd) ·
[Vector helpers](../reference/vectors.qmd#conditionals-and-na)
